channel.title: Walking with Jesus
channel.description: Morning, midday, and evening reflections on His life, teaching, and love.

item.title: Someone Did Touch Me
item.description: A Saturday morning in a pressing crowd, with a woman who hoped to stay hidden and a Savior who stopped everything to call her daughter.

item.title: Lord, Remember Me
item.description: A Friday evening beside a dying thief who had nothing left to offer, and the one-line prayer Jesus answered with a promise.

item.title: While He Was Still Far Off
item.description: A Friday midday pause with the son on the long road home, rehearsing his apology, and the father who couldn't wait for him to finish it.

item.title: When Jesus Saw Their Faith
item.description: A Friday morning on a crowded roof in Capernaum, with four friends who would not stop at the door and a man who couldn't walk to Jesus on his own.

item.title: Stay With Us, for It Is Toward Evening
item.description: A Thursday evening with Cleopas and his friend on the road to Emmaus — the simple invitation that opened their eyes, and still opens ours.

item.title: Consider the Lilies
item.description: A Thursday midday pause for the part of you that's already running numbers on tomorrow. Jesus points at a field of flowers and tells you something about your Father.

item.title: I Want To. Be Made Clean.
item.description: A Thursday morning with the man who knelt in the dust and wondered whether Jesus would even want him. Jesus answers with a touch before He answers with a word.

item.title: He Came to Jesus by Night
item.description: A Wednesday evening with Nicodemus, a careful man with big questions who came to Jesus after dark. For anyone who still has more questions than answers.

item.title: Today I Must Stay at Your House
item.description: A Wednesday midday with a short man in a sycamore tree. Jesus doesn't wait for Zacchaeus to clean up before He invites Himself over, and He doesn't wait for you either.

item.title: In the Fourth Watch
item.description: A Wednesday morning on a wind-tossed lake with Peter. Jesus comes in the last dark hours before sunrise, speaks into the fear, and holds out His hand to anyone who starts to sink.

item.title: Peace! Be Still!
item.description: An evening on the Sea of Galilee, a storm that came out of nowhere, and a Savior asleep in the boat. For the nights when you wonder if He cares.

item.title: What Are These Among So Many?
item.description: A Tuesday midday with a boy's packed lunch on a Galilean hillside. When what you have looks far too small for what the day is asking, Jesus says, bring it here.

item.title: What Do You Want Me to Do for You?
item.description: A Tuesday morning beside the Jericho road with blind Bartimaeus. Jesus stops for the one the crowd tried to hush, and asks a question worth carrying into the day.

item.title: He Took a Towel
item.description: A Monday evening at the supper table in John 13. Before you lie down with the dust of the day still on you, let Jesus kneel and wash what you carried in.

item.title: He Sat Down by the Well
item.description: A Monday midday with the woman at Jacob's well. She came at noon to avoid being seen, and found Someone who saw everything and stayed anyway.

item.title: At Your Word
item.description: A Monday morning with Peter at the shoreline. After a night of empty nets, Jesus asks for one more try — and the whole week can begin on His word instead of yesterday's results.

item.title: Your Faithfulness Every Night
item.description: Sunday evening does not need one more achievement. Psalm 92 invites a quieter close — giving thanks, and proclaiming God’s faithfulness into the night.

item.title: Remain in Me
item.description: Sunday midday can drift back into self-effort. Jesus offers a simpler way — stay connected to Him like a branch to the vine, where fruit grows from nearness, not strain.

item.title: Seek the Things Above
item.description: Sunday morning lifts your eyes. Colossians reminds the raised-with-Christ that the first direction of the day is upward — where Jesus is, and where your true life is kept.

item.title: In Peace I Will Lie Down
item.description: Saturday evening does not need a perfect ending before you can rest. Psalm 4 invites a quieter trust — lying down in peace because the Lord alone makes you dwell in safety.

item.title: Beside Still Waters
item.description: Saturday midday can still feel hurried even when the calendar softens. Psalm 23 invites a tired heart to be led beside still waters — where the Shepherd restores what the week has spent.

item.title: He Who Keeps You Will Not Slumber
item.description: Friday evening invites a different kind of trust — not that you will stay awake to manage everything, but that the Lord who keeps you never nods off.

item.title: Come Away and Rest Awhile
item.description: Friday midday often finds us tired and unfinished. In Mark 6 Jesus invites worn disciples to step aside with Him — not after everything is done, but while the crowd still presses.

item.title: When I Awake, I Am Still with You
item.description: Friday morning does not begin with you finding God. Psalm 139 says something quieter and kinder — you wake, and He is already there.

item.title: Peace I Leave With You
item.description: As Thursday evening settles, Jesus does not offer the world’s thin calm. He leaves His own peace — a gift that steadies troubled and fearful hearts.

item.title: One Thing Is Needed
item.description: Midday often multiplies tasks and noise. In Luke 10 Jesus gently redirects a busy heart toward the one thing that holds — Himself.

item.title: He Goes Before You
item.description: Thursday does not ask you to invent the day alone. Deuteronomy promises a Lord who walks ahead — present, faithful, and already at work in what you cannot yet see.

item.title: Come to the Waters
item.description: Isaiah’s morning invitation is not a pep talk — it is a welcome to thirsty people. Grace still meets us where we are empty, and Jesus still says come.

item.title: Be Our Arm Every Morning
item.description: Isaiah teaches a simple morning prayer — asking God not for a private escape from Tuesday, but for His strength to meet whatever the day actually holds.

item.title: Before the Day Crowds In
item.description: Mark shows Jesus rising early to pray — not to impress heaven, but to meet the Father before the day’s noise arrives. Monday can begin that way too.

item.title: Very Early on the First Day
item.description: Before the week asks anything of you, the Gospels open Sunday with a quiet fact — disciples walking toward a tomb, and a risen Lord who had already gone ahead.

item.title: As Sure as the Dawn
item.description: Hosea invites a tired heart not to invent its own morning, but to press on toward a God whose coming is as reliable as the light that finds the sky.

item.title: Give Us This Day
item.description: Before the calendar fills every pocket of attention, Jesus teaches a simpler morning prayer — asking the Father for today’s bread, not yesterday’s regret or tomorrow’s dread.

item.title: The Sunrise Shall Visit Us
item.description: Zechariah’s song names a mercy that does not wait for us to climb — the sunrise of God’s tender kindness visiting us from on high in Jesus.

item.title: Joy Comes with the Morning
item.description: Psalm 30 does not deny the night — it promises that weeping is not the last word, and that morning can carry a joy God Himself restores.

item.title: In the Morning I Watch
item.description: Psalm 5 offers a quiet morning practice — not only speaking to God, but preparing our hearts and watching for Him with trust.

item.title: Morning by Morning He Awakens
item.description: Before we speak into the day, Isaiah 50 offers a quieter gift — an ear awakened by God, ready to hear mercy and learn trust.

item.title: Satisfy Us in the Morning
item.description: Before the day asks for productivity, Psalm 90 asks for something deeper — a heart filled with God’s steadfast love at dawn.

item.title: Let Me Hear in the Morning
item.description: Before the day fills with noise, Psalm 143 asks for one first word — God’s steadfast love spoken into the quiet of dawn.

item.title: Come and Have Breakfast
item.description: At daybreak by the sea, Jesus welcomes tired disciples with a fire, a meal, and a mercy that arrives before they have a plan.

item.title: While It Was Still Dark
item.description: Mary comes to the tomb before sunrise — and finds that Jesus meets us in the grey hour when hope still feels unfinished.

item.title: New Every Morning
item.description: Before the day fills up, a quiet word from Lamentations — mercies that do not run out, and a Savior who meets us at dawn.

item.title: Stay With Us
item.description: Evening light on the Emmaus road — recognition, burning hearts, and the joy of remaining with the risen Jesus.

item.title: Take My Yoke
item.description: Midday rest for the weary — Jesus’ invitation in Matthew 11 to exchange our heavy loads for His gentle yoke.

item.title: Come and See
item.description: Jesus’ gentle invitation in John 1 — curiosity, encounter, and the beginning of discipleship.
